# autonomy

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
*The envelope and orchestrator of verifiably: what may run unattended*

What may run unattended, under what tier, and how the next research action is chosen: the run baseline and dispositions, tiers as write-class permits, the actor sandbox and session ledger, behavioural profiles and the versioned priority function. It drives science's commands as tools and holds no private kernel access. Built: tiers, the closing check, the sandbox, and autonomy run's launch side.

## Usage

```sh
autonomy run --tier <report-only|coordination|mints> [--route KIND=FAMILY]... \
  [--lease SECONDS] [--report-fd N] [--model-route NAME] -- <actor argv>
```

The actor gets `autonomy run`'s fds 0, 1 and 2, so each must be a pipe, a connected
`AF_UNIX` stream socket or `/dev/null`; a terminal or a file is refused. `autonomy run`
never reads stdin or writes stdout, help included, and its diagnostics on stderr are
for a person. At a terminal, run it as

```sh
(set -o pipefail; autonomy run --tier report-only -- <actor argv> </dev/null 2>&1 | cat -v)
```

`pipefail` keeps its exit code, which a pipeline would otherwise replace with `cat`'s:

| Exit | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | `clean` |
| 3 | `quarantined` |
| 4 | `unwired`, or stopped before its close, its run directory left for `run close` |
| 2 | refused before a run directory exists: a configuration, stdio or usage error |

Until science's run endpoint exists, every run that passes its checks closes
`unwired`. A program learns its run from `--report-fd`: one JSON line with the run's
id and directory, then one with its disposition and exit code
(`docs/specs/2026-10-12-envelope-design.md`, decision 12).

### The model route

An actor has no network of its own. `--model-route NAME` gives it one path out: a
proxy on `VERIFIABLY_MODEL_URL` (`http://127.0.0.1:4780`) that forwards only the
route's operations to its one upstream and adds the provider credential there. The
actor never holds the credential. Point the harness at that URL with a placeholder
key. For pi, that is a provider `baseUrl` in its models.json:

```json
{"providers": {"anthropic": {"baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:4780", "apiKey": "placeholder"}}}
```

That configuration only directs pi. The proxy enforces the route whatever the actor
does to it (decision 13). The route is a TOML file at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/verifiably-autonomy/routes/NAME.toml`:

```toml
api = "anthropic-messages"
upstream = "https://api.anthropic.com"
max_request_bytes = 8000000
forward_headers = ["anthropic-version", "anthropic-beta", "content-type", "accept", "user-agent"]

[header_tokens]
anthropic-version = ["2023-06-01"]
anthropic-beta = ["fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14", "interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14",
                  "mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01", "thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01",
                  "inline-tools-2026-09-15"]

[credential]
file = "/home/you/.config/verifiably-autonomy/credentials/anthropic"  # 0600, yours, one link
header = "x-api-key"

[[operations]]
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/messages"
queries = ["beta=true"]
models = ["claude-haiku-5-5"]
fields = ["model", "messages", "system", "max_tokens", "stream", "tools", "tool_choice",
          "thinking", "temperature", "metadata", "stop_sequences", "top_p", "top_k",
          "output_config"]
block_types = ["text", "image", "tool_use", "tool_result", "thinking", "redacted_thinking"]
source_types = ["base64"]
```

What the route leaves out, the proxy refuses with a `403` that names the code, for
example `body-refused` for an MCP server or a URL image source. `just live-egress
NAME` runs pi through the proxy to the real API once and prints what the proxy
recorded, including any beta token pi sends that the route does not list. The example
is what pi 1.1.0 needed on 2026-10-17. Never list `fallbacks` in `fields`: it names
other models, which the proxy does not check against `models`.

## Documentation

- [User and autonomy layer design](https://github.com/verifiably/beliefs/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-user-and-autonomy-layer-design.md)
  — the governing design, in the kernel repository: §7 is this layer, §8 orders the
  sub-projects. Work here starts at sub-project #6, the envelope, after the command
  framework, and ends with #7, the loop and the priority function (`science.priority.v1`).
- This repository's own designs and plans are under [docs/specs](docs/specs) and
  [docs/plans](docs/plans); the envelope's design is
  `docs/specs/2026-10-12-envelope-design.md`.
- This layer is split from `science` on code-lineage independence: the envelope must
  not share a package with the surface it constrains, so its only seam is `science`'s
  commands as tools.
